Der Schwerpunkt deiner Arbeit liegt auf Fördermitteln und der Suche nach neuen Finanzierungsmöglichkeiten für Kopfsachen. Gleichzeitig arbeitest du eng mit unseren Standorten sowie den Teams für Wirkung und Kommunikation zusammen. Der Schwerpunkt deiner Arbeit liegt auf Fördermitteln und der Suche nach neuen Finanzierungsmöglichkeiten für Kopfsachen. Gleichzeitig arbeitest du eng mit unseren Standorten sowie den Teams für Wirkung und Kommunikation zusammen. 

  • Arbeitsort: Berlin 
  • Arbeitszeit: 80 % / 32 Stunden
  • Start: 01.11.2026
  • Befristung: zunächst auf ein Jahr
Wir suchen eine proaktive, strukturierte und kommunikationsstarke Persönlichkeit, die erste praktische Erfahrung oder Berührungspunkte im Fundraising und insbesondere mit Förderanträgen mitbringt. Du musst noch kein*e Fundraising-Expert*in sein: Wichtig ist uns, dass du Lust hast, dich schnell in die Fördermittellandschaft einzuarbeiten, Verantwortung zu übernehmen und dich fachlich weiterzuentwickeln.


Deine Mission

Als Fundraising & Partnerships Manager*in trägst du maßgeblich dazu bei, die Finanzierung unserer Arbeit langfristig zu sichern und weiterzuentwickeln. Du recherchierst passende Fördermöglichkeiten, entwickelst überzeugende Anträge und Berichte und gehst gleichzeitig aktiv auf die Suche nach neuen Fundraising-Chancen. Dabei wartest du nicht darauf, dass Möglichkeiten zu uns kommen, sondern hast Freude daran, neue Kontakte, Programme und Netzwerke zu erschließen. Gleichzeitig sorgst du dafür, dass unsere Standorte bei Finanzierungsfragen gut unterstützt werden und unsere Förderpartner*innen nachvollziehen können, welche Wirkung ihre Unterstützung ermöglicht.


Deine Aufgaben

  • Du recherchierst relevante Förderprogramme, Ausschreibungen und potenzielle Förderpartner*innen und identifizierst aktiv neue Finanzierungsmöglichkeiten für Kopfsachen.
  • Du entwickelst und schreibst überzeugende Förderanträge und verantwortest die dazugehörigen Förderberichte.
  • Du behältst laufende Anträge, Fristen und Anforderungen im Blick und sorgst für eine zuverlässige und strukturierte Begleitung der Schnittstellen. 
  • Gemeinsam mit dem Fundraising-Team entwickelst du neue Ansätze für unsere Finanzierung weiter und bringst Strukturen und Prozesse ein, die unsere Fundraising-Arbeit effizienter machen.
  • Du bist Ansprechpartner*in für unsere Standortleitungen bei Fragen rund um Finanzierung, Fördermöglichkeiten und Partnerschaften und unterstützt sie bei regionalen Förderanträgen.
  • Du sorgst für einen guten Austausch zwischen Fundraising und unseren Standorten und entwickelst hilfreiche Strukturen, Vorlagen und Ressourcen für die Zusammenarbeit.
  • Du arbeitest an unserem Wirkungs- und Jahresbericht mit und bereitest wissenschaftliche Ergebnisse, Kennzahlen und Wirkungsdaten verständlich für unsere Förderpartner*innen auf.
  • Dafür arbeitest du eng mit den Teams für Wirkung und Kommunikation zusammen und sorgst dafür, dass relevante Informationen für Berichte gut zusammengeführt werden.


Dein Profil

  • Du hast erste praktische Erfahrungen oder Berührungspunkte mit Fundraising, Förderanträgen, Projektfinanzierung oder vergleichbaren Themen gesammelt 
  • Idealerweise kennst du die Fördermittellandschaft in Deutschland bereits und hast ein erstes Verständnis dafür, worauf es bei guten Förderanträgen und Berichten ankommt. 
  • Du kannst dich schnell in neue Themen einarbeiten und Verantwortung für deine Aufgaben übernehmen.
  • Auch als Quereinsteiger*in bist du bei uns herzlich willkommen, wenn du relevante Erfahrungen aus Bereichen wie Projektmanagement, Kommunikation, Non-Profit-Arbeit, Wissenschaft oder öffentlicher Förderung mitbringst. 
  • Du arbeitest selbstständig, strukturiert und zuverlässig und behältst auch bei mehreren parallelen Projekten und Fristen den Überblick.
  • Du schreibst gerne und kannst komplexe Inhalte klar, verständlich und Zielgruppengerecht vermitteln.
  • Du bist proaktiv, gehst offen auf Menschen zu und hast Freude daran, neue Kontakte und Finanzierungsmöglichkeiten zu erschließen.
  • Du arbeitest gerne mit unterschiedlichen Teams zusammen und kommunizierst sicher mit internen und externen Ansprechpartner*innen.
  • Du verfügst über sehr gute Deutschkenntnisse in Wort und Schrift (C2).
  • Du bist motiviert, unsere Mission mitzugestalten und mit deiner Arbeit konkrete Wirkung für die mentale Gesundheit junger Menschen zu ermöglichen.


Unser Angebot

  • Eine bedeutungsvolle Mission: Du arbeitest an einer Aufgabe, die wirklich einen Unterschied im Leben junger Menschen macht.
  • Gestaltungsfreiraum: Bei uns kannst du deine Ideen einbringen, ausprobieren und direkt umsetzen.
  • Flexible Arbeitszeiten & hybrides Arbeitsmodell: Arbeite, wo und wie du am besten wirken kannst – im Impact Hub Berlin oder im Homeoffice.
  • Innovatives Umfeld: Teil eines agilen Social Start-ups mit viel Raum für Kreativität und Eigenverantwortung.
  • Interdisziplinäre Zusammenarbeit: Lerne von Expert*innen aus Psychologie, Bildung, Fundraising und Kommunikation an mehreren Standorten.
  • Begleitung & Feedback: Du wirst eng betreut, erhältst regelmäßiges Feedback und kannst dich fachlich wie persönlich weiterentwickeln.
Wir ermutigen ausdrücklich alle qualifizierten Personen, sich bei uns zu bewerben – insbesondere Menschen mit Migrationsgeschichte, BIPoC, Menschen der LGBTQIA+ Community sowie Menschen mit Behinderungen. Wir freuen uns auch auf deine Bewerbung, wenn du nicht alle Anforderungen zu 100 % erfüllst.

title: Systems Integration & QA Engineer (All genders)
description:
About Us

STARK is a new kind of defence technology company revolutionising the way autonomous systems are deployed across multiple domains. We design, develop, and manufacture high-performance unmanned systems that are software-defined, mass-scalable, and cost-effective — providing operators with a decisive edge in contested environments.

We are focused on delivering deployable, high-performance systems — not future promises. In a time of rising threats, STARK is bolstering the technological edge of NATO Allies and their Partners to deter aggression and defend Europe, today.


About the team

Mission Simulation is STARK’s digital proving ground — the tactical environment where our entire ecosystem of UAVs, surface vessels, and EW systems converges. The Mission Simulation team is a small, specialized group based in Munich, working closely with our platform and C2 teams to integrate all multi-domain assets into high-fidelity, Software-in-the-Loop simulators.

We move fast, ship realistic environments, and build for three core purposes: rigorous testing, high-stakes demos, and tactical training. There is no room for gamification. We simulate the reality of combat — from complex swarm logic to EW degradation — ensuring that developers can fail fast, and real soldiers can train safely before hitting the battlefield.

Notre mission ⚖️

Chez Doctrine, nous construisons le leader de l’IA juridique en Europe.

Notre conviction ? Le droit ne doit pas être ralenti par des tâches répétitives. Il doit être augmenté par une IA spécialisée, conçue pour comprendre, analyser et produire du raisonnement juridique avec un haut niveau d’exigence.

Notre ambition ? Permettre aux professionnels du droit de gagner en fiabilité, en efficacité et en sérénité, grâce à une plateforme unique, exhaustive et sécurisée.

Aujourd’hui, 27 000 professionnels du droit, répartis dans cinq pays (France, Italie, Allemagne, Espagne, Luxembourg), nous font confiance.

Notre développement est guidé par une approche claire : une vision globale, ancrée dans une compréhension fine des spécificités locales.

Derrière cette ambition, une équipe d’environ 250 personnes, réunies autour d’un même objectif : accompagner les juristes et avocats à toutes les étapes de leur travail, de l’analyse à la rédaction.

Et nous n’en sommes qu’au début.


Sujet de stage

Doctrine développe des workflows dédiés aux professionnels du droit pour accélérer et améliorer la gestion de leurs dossiers. Parmi eux, Jobexit accompagne les avocats et juristes en droit social dans la simulation de ruptures du contrat de travail, notamment en calculant les indemnités de départ, les indemnités en cas de contentieux, le calendrier de sortie et les allocations chômage.

Dans un litige, un salarié peut demander plusieurs choses à la fois : des salaires impayés, une indemnité de licenciement, des dommages et intérêts, etc. L'objectif du stage est de permettre à l'utilisateur de saisir et d'organiser toutes ces demandes dans l'application, pour mieux estimer les montants en jeu, préparer la négociation avec la partie adverse et générer automatiquement le récapitulatif final destiné au juge. Ceci peut inclure :

  • Concevoir une interface pour ajouter, modifier et réordonner les demandes d'un dossier, chacune avec son montant, son unité de calcul et son ordre
  • Modéliser les dépendances entre demandes (une demande qui ne s'applique que si une autre est refusée par exemple)
  • Calculer et afficher les montants (du coût pour l’employeur au net empoché par le salarié), pour aider l'utilisateur à évaluer les risques
  • Générer automatiquement un document de synthèse clair et structuré, prêt à être intégré dans les conclusions écrites de l'avocat
  • Et d'autres fonctionnalités !

Le ou la stagiaire participera à la compréhension du besoin utilisateur autour de ces outils (en collaboration avec les équipes produit et les juristes) et à la définition des solutions techniques (en collaboration avec les équipes techniques). Il ou elle rejoindra l’équipe Jobexit et participera également au chapter web (regroupement de tous les développeurs fullstack de l’entreprise).

 


Les à-côtés du poste 👁️
Le ou la stagiaire participera comme tous les ingénieurs à son chapter (réuni 2 fois par mois) dont le but est de :
  • Partager des connaissances entre ses membres (amélioration continue, bonnes pratiques)
  • Proposer des améliorations (nouveaux outils et processus)
  • Aider ses membres en fonction de leurs besoins

    • Ce qui t'attend si tu rejoins Doctrine 🤝

    • Contribuer à un projet ambitieux, avec un impact réel et positif sur la société : rendre le droit plus accessible et plus ouvert.
    • Un onboarding très complet permettant une intégration et une montée en compétence rapides.
    • Une aventure dans laquelle la formation et le partage des connaissances font partis du quotidien.
    • Rejoindre une entreprise avec une vie d’équipe riche et dynamique : conférences, team-buildings, déjeuner, offsite, afterwork, etc.

    Nos valeurs 🤝

    Chez Doctrine, nos 4 valeurs nous accompagnent au quotidien et dans notre ambition de faire bouger les choses.

    • Challenge the status quo : nous défendons les idées audacieuses qui contribuent à l’évolution de tout un secteur.
    • Liberty and responsibility : nous encourageons l’autonomie, l’impact de chacun·e et l’ownership.
    • Knowledge is power : l'information est au cœur de la mission de Doctrine, et nous cherchons constamment à progresser.
    • Release early, release often and listen to your customers : nous croyons au pouvoir de l’itération et à l’importance d’écouter en permanence notre marché, nos client·e·s et leurs problématiques.
     

    Nos avantages pour faire la différence ☀️

    🏡 Une politique de télétravail flexible permettant - selon les équipes - jusqu’à trois jours de télétravail par semaine.

    🌴 Une politique de congés flexibles

    🌱 Des opportunités concrètes de mobilité interne

    📚 Un vrai accent sur la formation individuelle et collective, avec un budget annuel de 750€ pour toute formation en lien avec ton poste - et des formations en équipe ou pour toute l'entreprise

    🏋️‍♀️ Un abonnement Gymlib pour les activités sportives et bien-être

    🧘 Un accès gratuit à la plateforme d'accompagnement à la santé mentale Moka.care et un accompagnement individuel allant jusqu’à 6 séances par an

    👩‍⚕️ Une assurance santé avec Alan

    💡 Des réductions et avantages négociés grâce à notre CSE via la plateforme Happypal

    🍏 Un équipement de travail neuf chez Apple

     

    Notre processus de recrutement 🚀

    • Un premier échange de 30 min avec l’un.e de nos Talent Acquisition Manager pour bien comprendre ton projet professionnel et te présenter ce qu'on construit chez Doctrine
    • Une rencontre d’1h avec ton/ta futur.e manager, pour détailler le poste et le scope de l’équipe, mais aussi répondre à toutes tes questions.
    • Un ou deux tests techniques pour évaluer concrètement tes compétences
    • Une venue dans nos bureaux pour : un déjeuner avec 3 personnes de différents départements chez Doctrine, pour te donner un aperçu de tes futur.e.s collègues ; un échange sur les valeurs de l’entreprise pour te partager notre vision, et une rencontre avec notre CEO, Guillaume.

Si cela peut vous rassurer, sachez que cette fiche de poste est indicative donc prenez la comme telle : c'est un guide, ni plus ni moins.

Les collections femme et homme font référence à l'art de vivre à la française et aux gestes universels de beauté, intégrant des influences allant de la photographie d'art aux arts décoratifs, en passant par le cinéma, la peinture et la sculpture.
 
Au fil des années, Jacquemus a mis en scène ses défilés dans des lieux uniques et inattendus, notamment une piscine parisienne, le Musée Picasso, un champ de lavande en Provence, un champ de blé aux abords de Paris, un marais salant en Camargue et une plage à Hawaï. Our mission is simple: to make self-custody accessible and give people the keys to their own financial futures. If you want to make a true impact, we want you to join us at Ledger.

 

At Ledger, we’re proud to be the global platform for digital assets and Web3, with over 20% of the world’s crypto assets secured through our Ledger devices. With our headquarters in Paris, and offices in Vierzon, Grenoble, Montpellier, London, Portland, Geneva, Zurich and Central Singapore, we have a team of around 600 professionals developing a variety of products and services to enable individuals and companies to securely buy, store, swap, grow and manage crypto assets – including the Ledger hardware wallets line with more than 7.5 millions units already sold in 200 countries.

 

The team:

You're joining as we reshape the People & Operations Experience team, which brings together ops, payroll, people tech, engagement and internal comms. That makes this a build-and-run role. You'll run payroll from day one and help design how the function works going forward, from processes to tooling to documentation.

 
 

The role

You'll take ownership of French payroll, starting with a proper handover from the colleague who runs it today and building towards running it independently. Alongside it, you'll look after the employee lifecycle: joiners, leavers and everything in between. It's real responsibility, with a team around you.

Your development goes in two directions: continuous improvement of how People Ops works, and a progressive move into Global Payroll (US, UK, Singapore) as your confidence and scope grow. Your arrival also creates room for the whole team to take on bigger things, and that includes you.

 

What you'll do

 

Own French payroll

  • Run the full monthly cycle: data collection, absences and leave, inputs, controls, validation and payslip checks

  • Prepare and submit statutory filings on time (URSSAF, DSN, IJSS/Net-entreprise and other mandatory declarations)

  • Manage variable pay and contractual changes, and build the VPI file for ADP Decidium

  • Work with Finance on transfer files, cost reporting, headcount tracking and variance analysis

  • Handle day to day equity payroll declarations (stock options / BSPCE) as you slowly build your expertise

  • Manage benefits, meal vouchers and provider relationships

  • Track regulatory changes and turn them into better processes

 

Run the employee lifecycle

  • Handle joiners and leavers: contracts, health insurance and transport registration, visa and absence data

  • Keep Workday data accurate and compliant

  • Help document and improve the processes being rebuilt, and contribute to cross-functional People projects

  • You'll work with Finance, Talent Acquisition, HRBPs, C&B and our provider ADP.

 

What you bring

  • 2–3 years of French payroll experience, with hands-on exposure to the monthly cycle and a readiness to own it

  • Solid knowledge of French social legislation (URSSAF, DSN) and experience with a payroll tool (ADP or similar)

  • Rigour: you close the month on time, without being chased

  • A builder's instinct: you document as you go and like making things work better

  • Comfort working in English in a multicultural team

  • Curiosity about international payroll and a real appetite to widen your scope

description:
About Scality

Scality builds data infrastructure software for enterprise AI, cyber resilience, and sovereign control at multi-petabyte to exabyte scale. Its AI Data Infrastructure platform reduces operational burden through AI-powered autonomous operations while aligning the right storage media, performance, and protection to each workload through human-approved lifecycle policies.
 
Built on CORE5 cyber resilience and open-code principles, Scality software delivers extreme performance, operational simplicity, and sustainable economics. 
 
The world's most demanding enterprises and government organizations depend on Scality to power AI initiatives, defend critical data, and build infrastructure that lasts for decades. Recognized as a leader by Gartner, Scality is where AI remembers, learns, and thinks. F
 
ollow us on LinkedIn. Visit www.scality.com and our blog.

About the role
Scality is looking for an experienced Demand Generation Campaign Manager to own our global campaign program. You plan, launch, and optimize the campaigns that generate qualified leads and opportunities across our enterprise and mid-market go to market in the Americas, EMEA, and Asia Pacific.
 
This is a hands-on role for a marketer who thinks strategically. You take a pipeline target, decide how to reach it, and run the campaigns that get there. You hold yourself to the numbers: leads and opportunities generated, conversion by stage, cost per lead and per opportunity, and channel efficiency. Most of the work is digital. You also run the campaigns around our webinars, trade shows, and partner programs, from promotion to lead follow up.
 
The main challenge is generating demand in a market that is changing fast. Buyers increasingly get their information from AI tools rather than the channels marketers have relied on, and gated content and volume downloads are losing their effect. This role needs the creativity to build demand where the old playbooks no longer work.

You own the campaign function in an international marketing team. You work closely with the Head of Growth, who runs paid media, SEO, and web, and with marketing operations and nurture. You work with the AMER field marketing manager and the EMEA regional marketing team on campaigns for their events and partner programs, and with product marketing on messaging and assets. You also work with sales, SDR, and partner teams in every region.

What you will be doing
  • Own the global campaign plan and calendar, translating pipeline targets into integrated campaigns across paid social, paid search, email, webinars, content syndication, and account-based marketing
  • Take each campaign from brief to launch: audience and targeting, offer, messaging with product marketing, landing pages and forms, promotion, lead routing, and reporting
  • Run campaigns for webinars, trade shows, field events, and partner programs, from promotion before the event to lead follow up after
  • Run the thought leadership and customer webinar program, from topic and speakers to registration, delivery, and follow up
  • Work with the Head of Growth on paid media strategy, spend allocation, and experimentation across LinkedIn, Google, and new channels
  • Build campaigns with marketing operations in HubSpot and Salesforce, and own campaign structure, naming, and attribution in Salesforce
  • Own weekly and monthly lead generation reporting to marketing and executive leadership: leads and opportunities against goal, conversion by stage, cost per lead and per opportunity, and spend by channel and region
  • Align with sales and SDR teams across regions on lead handoff, follow up, and pipeline acceleration
  • Manage campaign budgets and agencies, and prioritize spend against pipeline impact
  • Run experiments across audiences, offers, and channels to improve conversion and lower acquisition cost

    • What you bring to the table
  • Ten years or more of experience in lead generation, demand generation, or digital marketing, running integrated campaigns end to end
  • International experience: you have run campaigns across several regions, ideally including the US, and understand how buyers and channels differ by market
  • Experience in B2B enterprise software, ideally in storage, data management, backup, or adjacent data infrastructure markets
  • A track record of campaigns that produced measurable pipeline, with the numbers to back it up
  • Hands-on experience with paid social and paid search, and with webinar and event campaigns 
  • Strong command of HubSpot and Salesforce and of campaign analytics
  • The ability to shape a plan from a pipeline target while staying hands on in execution
  • The creativity to generate demand where buyers rely on AI over traditional channels and gated content no longer carries the funnel
  • Native or near-native English, written and spoken. You write campaign copy for US and international audiences
  • Comfort working with colleagues across time zones, with regular overlap with the US team in the afternoon

    • Life at Scality
  • We offer careers with an opportunity to bridge international borders, an intensely fun environment with smart people.
  • We encourage promotion and elevation through training and development programs.
  • We care for our employees through company supported programs such as sports and wellness programs, social responsibility programs, and generous benefits packages.
  • We support team building and get together events across all of our locations around the world.
  • Life at Scality is exhilarating. Our internal motto is: work hard, play hard, eat well and amaze the customer!

title: Quantum Information Scientist - Architecture & Performance
description:
About Quandela:

Quandela is a global leader in quantum computing, designing, building, and delivering cutting-edge quantum solutions for research and industry. Its offerings include the most energy-efficient quantum computers for data centers, full-stack quantum computing solutions accessible via the cloud, and algorithm access services for academic and industrial customers.
Following a pragmatic, step-by-step roadmap, Quandela has been deploying industrial-grade systems since 2023 while developing future generations of fault-tolerant quantum computers capable of scaling through the integration of thousands of photonic components. Quandela is committed to making quantum computing accessible to all in order to address the most complex industrial and societal challenges.
Learn more at: Quandela | Leading Photonic Quantum Computing Solutions

Our ambition is to build large-scale fault-tolerant quantum computers capable of solving problems beyond the reach of classical computation. 

Getting there will require several generations of intermediate architectures. Choosing the right ones means understanding what can be built, what these systems can compute and how efficiently they can do so.

About this position:

You will join Quandela’s Quantum Information team within Architecture, working on the evaluation and design of our near- and mid-term quantum architectures. 

Your role will sit between quantum theory, computational capability and real hardware constraints. You will develop methods to evaluate architecture concepts, understand their performance and limitations, and help guide future architecture choices.

Depending on your background, you may draw on complexity theory, quantum learning theory, quantum-system characterisation, benchmarking or related areas. You will work closely with our Device Physics, FTQC and Q.Algorithms Team.

Requirements

What you'll do:

As a Quantum Information Scientist working on Architecture & Performance, you will: 

  • Evaluate and compare the capabilities and limitations of near- and mid-term quantum architectures. 
  • Draw on methods from complexity theory, benchmarking, characterisation and related fields to assess different architecture designs. 
  • Incorporate realistic noise, native operations and physical constraints into your analyses. 
  • Investigate when and how different architectures could provide meaningful computational capabilities or advantages. 
  • Develop scientific models and numerical tools to explore architecture-performance trade-offs. 
  • Study how architecture choices interact with algorithms, resource requirements and QEC strategies. 
  • Progressively propose and lead new research projects around architecture design and performance. 

You will work across our Architecture team and Algorithms and Applications team, connecting questions from the physical layer to computational capability and potential applications. 
-

How you'll grow:

During your first 3–6 months 
Become familiar with Quandela’s technologies, architecture roadmap and ongoing research while contributing to existing evaluation and performance studies. 

Within 1 year 
Take increasing ownership of architecture studies, compare different concepts and bring your own scientific perspective to the team. 

Longer term 
Lead exploratory research projects, propose new architecture directions and contribute to shaping Quandela’s future architecture roadmap.

--

What we're looking for:
We are looking for a scientist with a strong theoretical background in quantum computing, scientific autonomy and an interest in connecting different layers of the quantum-computing stack.

Must-have 

  • PhD in Quantum Information, Quantum Computing, Physics, Mathematics, Computer Science or a closely related field. 
  • Strong expertise in one or more relevant areas, such as quantum complexity theory, quantum learning theory, quantum-system characterisation, performance analysis or quantum algorithms. 
  • Experience connecting theoretical or computational questions with realistic implementation, hardware or experimental constraints. 
  • Ability to assess the capabilities and limitations of quantum systems or architectures. 
  • Experience with scientific modelling, numerical simulation and Python-based scientific computing. 
  • Scientific autonomy and ability to structure open-ended research problems.
  • Collaborative and personable, with the ability to communicate ideas clearly to people from other fields of expertise.
  • Professional English. 

Important, but you can grow here 

  • Quantum Error Correction and early fault-tolerant architectures.
  • Hardware-aware algorithm or architecture design. 
  • Quantum benchmarking and performance metrics. 
  • Noise modelling. 
  • Resource and computational-cost analysis. 
  • Collaboration with experimental or hardware-oriented quantum-computing teams. 

Bonus 

  • Quantum compilation or native-gate-aware circuit design. 
  • Photonic quantum computing. 
  • Resource estimation. 
  • Experience comparing quantum approaches against strong classical baselines. 
  • Previous ownership of collaborative research projects. 

You do not need to cover every topic above. We welcome both candidates with postdoctoral or equivalent industrial R&D experience and strong recent PhDs demonstrating scientific autonomy.

Benefits

Join a growing quantum-computing company and contribute directly to the research behind future generations of quantum architectures. 

  • Explore open scientific questions grounded in real hardware constraints. 
  • Work across Quantum Information, Device Physics, FTQC and Algorithms. 
  • Take ownership of broad and exploratory research projects. 
  • Contribute to the scientific directions of a growing team. 

Plus: 

  • Competitive compensation aligned with your experience and level of responsibility. 
  • Company savings plan.
  • 100% health coverage through Alan. 
  • Transport reimbursement or sustainable mobility bonus. 
  • Swile meal vouchers. 
  • Access to Gymlib. 

Process 

  • Talent Acquisition interview, 30–45 min
  • Interview with Quantum Information hiring manager, 30-45 min
  • Presentation of previous research work and discussion with members of the theory team 
  • Reference checks 
  • Technical discussion based on a scientific paper or research topic
  • Offer 

For the technical exercise, you may be asked to explore scientific material outside your direct area of expertise and discuss how you would connect it to a broader architecture problem.

Demain, notre console recevra des milliards de requêtes. Votre mission : faire en sorte qu’elle tienne, et qu’elle reste rapide. Arkane Cloud crée un poste de Développeur Full Stack, à 80 % back-end, pour bâtir une plateforme taillée pour la charge.

 

Notre société

Arkane Cloud est un Cloud Service Provider lyonnais qui rend la puissance de calcul IA accessible, abordable et disponible en quelques minutes. Grâce à notre propre infrastructure composée de centaines de GPU, startups, chercheurs et entreprises déploient leurs modèles d’IA sans se battre avec la technique.

  • Jusqu’à 70 % d’économies par rapport à un hyperscaler

  • Une plateforme Plug & Play prête en moins de 3 minutes.

Notre ambition : bâtir un acteur européen de référence de l’infrastructure IA.

 

Pourquoi ce poste ?

Notre console est le point d’entrée de nos clients : c’est là qu’ils déploient et pilotent leurs ressources GPU. Avec l’essor de l’IA, elle va devoir absorber une très grande quantité de requêtes. Nous créons ce poste pour la rendre robuste face aux pics de charge, développer les API qui la font tourner et installer les bonnes pratiques qui permettront à l’équipe de grandir. Votre temps se partage à 80 % sur le back-end et 20 % sur le front-end.

 

Vos missions

• Tenir les pics de charge : une architecture qui absorbe le trafic sans ralentir.

• Développer nos API en Node.js : performantes, sécurisées, documentées.

• Installer les bonnes pratiques : revues de code, tests automatisés, monitoring.

• Optimiser la base de données PostgreSQL.

• Faire évoluer l’interface de la console en React.js (environ 20 % du temps).

 

Vos 6 premiers mois

1er mois : Prise en main de la console et de son architecture, premier audit de performance, premières mises en production.

3 mois : Tests de charge en place, premiers points de blocage corrigés, bonnes pratiques formalisées.

6 mois : Console capable d’absorber n'importe quelle montée en charge, monitoring et alertes opérationnels.

 

Votre expérience

• 5 ans ou plus en développement, avec une dominante back-end.

• Une expérience sur une plateforme grand public ou à fort trafic.

Vos expertises

• Node.js : conception d’API robustes et performantes.

• React.js : à l’aise pour faire évoluer une interface existante.

• Montée en charge : cache, files d’attente, tests de charge, scalabilité.

Un vrai plus :

Playwright, Grafana, connaissance du cloud ou des infrastructures GPU.

Votre façon de travailler : rigoureux sur la qualité, pragmatique, à l’aise pour partager vos pratiques avec l’équipe.

 

Pourquoi nous rejoindre

• Un vrai défi technique : S'assurer de la robuste de la plateforme lors des montées en charge

• Un impact direct : Vos choix d’architecture façonnent la plateforme.

• Des standards à poser : c’est vous qui fixez le niveau d’exigence de l’équipe.

• Au cœur de l’IA : vos API pilotent une infrastructure GPU dédiée à l’IA.

 

Package et avantages

• Télétravail 3 jours par semaine, présence au bureau de Lyon le mercredi et le jeudi

• Mutuelle à 100 %, tickets restaurant, RTT (Convention Syntec)

• Choix du matériel (PC ou Mac) & BSPCE

 

Arkane Cloud s’engage pour la diversité : nous étudions toutes les candidatures, sans distinction de genre, d’âge, d’origine ou de handicap.

 

Compensation: €45K – €65K

title: Product Marketing Manager in Legal Tech (Zurich)
description:
Description

Legal AI content is turning into a commodity. Every vendor ships the same AI-generated blog posts and the same generic battlecards. We are transitioning into an AI-native company ourselves, and that changes what this role has to be. You would sit in the marketing department with a dotted line to the product department, but not as a traditional product marketer who ships a few blog posts and calls it enablement. Not as a pure thinker who never touches a sales deck. Instead, as one person who owns our voice and turns it into everything the company needs to win: the thesis that gets us cited, the sales slide that closes next week’s deal, and the briefing that gets a General Counsel to say yes.

You will use AI tooling and agents to cover ground that used to take a small team, so you can spend your own time on the part that cannot be delegated: the thinking, the judgment, and the writing that actually changes someone’s mind.


Your mission

1. Product Marketing & Market Intelligence 

  • Drive go-to-market impact for launches and expansion, from plan to execution.

  • Own deep knowledge of our ICP and competitive landscape, and feed it back into the product and sales strategy.

  • Bring market and customer truth back to Product so we build what actually matters.

  • Work across Product, Marketing, Sales and leadership. You don’t sit in a silo.

2. Positioning, Narrative & Thought Leadership 

  • Own positioning: define what Legartis stands for, against which alternatives, for which buyer.

  • Develop and defend clear, evidence-backed points of view on where Legal AI is going. Not generic AI-created opinions, but real positions based on customer and buyer research (interviews with General Counsel, CFOs, legal operations leaders).

  • Conceive flagship studies and thought leadership content. Direct AI tools to help you scale production while you own the substance and the voice.

  • Own our thought leadership channels, including video, and decide what gets said. Write what can’t be delegated: founder posts, executive bylines, keynote scripts, board-level memos.

3. Sales & Customer-Facing Enablement 

  • Build the sales slides, briefings, one-pagers and competitive battlecards that make Sales and Customer Success more effective in every conversation.

  • Translate positioning and research into materials for specific deals, verticals and executive-level conversations.

  • Work directly with Sales and CS to find out what’s missing in the field. Build case studies and customer proof points that Sales actually uses, not ones that sit in a folder.

What We Want to Achieve Together

In 6 months: a flagship study that gets cited by competitors and customers. Sales armed with materials that actually get used in deals. A clear Legartis position that everyone in the company can repeat in 30 seconds.

In 12 months: Legartis recognized as one of the leading European voices on Legal AI, with a content and enablement engine, you plus the AI tools you direct, that outproduces companies with five times the headcount.


Your profile

  • Proven strategist: demonstrated success creating and executing marketing strategies.

  • Storyteller: you craft compelling materials about complex AI products for non-technical audiences.

  • Clear communicator: exceptional written and verbal communication with a strong visual sensibility.

  • Impact-driven: comfortable with experimentation and interpreting both quantitative and qualitative data.

  • AI-savvy: crafty with AI tools and automations — you use them daily and keep exploring what's new.

  • A track record where writing and thinking were central: journalism, industry or analyst research, strategy consulting, or senior product marketing with real strategic ownership. 4+ years in marketing, product marketing or a comparable strategic role at a SaaS company. Classic PMM experience (positioning, GTM, enablement) is a strong plus, not a hard requirement, if your thinking and writing are strong enough.

  • Fluent German and English, executive-level writing in both.


Why us?

  • Real editorial ownership over our voice and our position, not a content calendar handed down from someone else.

  • A platform to build your own visible profile as a voice in Legal AI.

  • Modern office in Leipzig or Berlin, hybrid setup, with regular presence in Zürich and team events such as hiking, dinners and offsites.

  • Employee Stock Ownership Plan (ESOP) participation.

  • Competitive salary, based on experience and seniority.


Process

  1. 30 min with our People & Operations Manager: cultural fit, understanding the role and your expectations.

  2. Positioning conversation with our Head of Product: bring a point of view on Legal AI and be ready to defend it live.

  3. Case study: show us something you’ve written or built, and how you’d turn it into a sales-ready asset.

  4. Meet the team in the office.

  5. Decision: if it’s mutual, we welcome you to the team!

How to Apply

Send us your CV, two or three writing or work samples you’re proud of, and a short note answering: what’s your sharpest point of view on where Legal AI is heading, and what’s the evidence?

title: Legal AI Engineer (Zurich)
description:
Description

Legartis is on a mission: to unlock legal work at scale.

We set the standard for AI-powered contract work by offering a platform that changes how legal teams work, from drafting through negotiation to completion. We are now looking for the person who turns what customers actually need into what our AI actually does.

Joining Legartis is not taking a job, you take ownership. We are a team of product builders and lawyers, who do not chase hype; we build substance. If you are a lawyer who builds, someone who has stopped waiting for better tools and started making them, this is your moment and your place.

Send us your CV, a short note on why Legartis, and links to anything you have built or published.


Your mission

Most companies split this seat across three teams, and that split is exactly the problem. The person who hears the customer describe their workflow should be the person who writes the requirement, and the person who writes the requirement should be able to build the first version themselves. That is you.

1. You translate customer reality into engineering requirements — and into revenue. You sit in customer and expert calls alongside Sales, not as a note-taker but as the person who understands the legal work. In trials and hackathons you coach hands-on: the customer drives, you navigate, and they create the first "wow" moment themselves. When they say "that won't work for us" or "we'll build it ourselves", you answer with a concrete path (a workaround, a workflow, the honest maintenance cost of the alternative) and you leave every conversation with a next step: trial licenses, a hackathon, a scoped rollout. Then you pull out the workflow: what actually happens, in what order, where it breaks, what the customer would pay to never do again. And you write the spec, edge cases, and acceptance criteria that Engineering can build against.

2. You build the skills yourself. You write, test, and ship agent skills and playbooks that solve real customer workflows. You build the evaluation frameworks and test sets that prove they got better rather than just different. When the AI fails on a clause, you diagnose why, at the prompt and context level, and you either fix it or hand Engineering a diagnosis precise enough to act on.

3. You make it repeatable, and therefore sellable. Anything you build once for one customer, you turn into something Sales and Customer Success can run without you. Standard demo environments. A skill library they can reach for. Onboarding that lands in days rather than months. Where Customer Success needs legal depth you step in, fix it, and turn the fix into something the team can handle alone next time. Your success is measured by how rarely you need to be in the room, and by what happens to adoption and expansion when you are not.

4. You are the legal authority in the building. Legal and compliance questions land with you: contract reviews, customer security and data protection questions, the occasional in-house matter which makes roughly ten to fifteen percent of your time. You use our own product to do it, and you tell us honestly when it is not good enough.


Your profile

The person we picture. There is a name emerging for what we are describing, and it is not "lawyer who is good with computers". It is legal quant: a lawyer who builds their own tooling to practise law, rather than waiting for a vendor to ship it. The distinction that matters to us: plenty of lawyers now use AI. A legal quant builds with it. They look at a workflow and ask how to redesign it from first principles to get the best possible outcome, rather than making the existing process incrementally faster.

A note on how we are weighting this role. Three capabilities make someone exceptional here: commercial instinct, legal depth, and technical ability to build. The ideal candidate has all three. We know that person is rare, and we are not going to pretend otherwise by writing a wish list and hoping. So for this role we weight the technical evidence most heavily, because it is the hardest of the three to teach on the job.

If you believe you genuinely combine all three, we want to talk to you regardless of how neatly your CV matches the bullets below. Say so in your note and tell us what you have built and what you have sold.

1. Technical track record. You have built things and they exist and ideally you have published some of it. You are fluent with LLMs the way a practitioner is fluent, not a spectator: you know how context windows fail you or why a prompt stopped working. When something breaks you go into the system rather than around it. Scripting, Git, and APIs are a strong plus.

2. Legal foundation. A law degree with a commercial-contracts focus: German-qualified (Bachelor, Master, or Staatsexamen) or an equivalent qualification from another jurisdiction. No bar admission required, no second Staatsexamen required. What we need: you have worked hands-on with German commercial contracts, drafting, reviewing, and negotiating them, and you can hold a conversation with a General Counsel as a peer.

3. Commercial and entrepreneurial track record. You have carried commercial responsibility for something of your own: a freelance client base, a legal tech product, or a company you started. You know what it takes to win a client from a standing start and why "they did not understand the value" is never the customer's fault. If instead you have supported enterprise sales teams in demos, pilots, and expert calls, tell us what you changed about the outcome.

You prioritise by impact, you are comfortable deciding without permission, and you would rather ship something imperfect this week than something elegant next quarter.

4. Language. Excellent German and English. German is non-negotiable: our customers are DACH legal teams and the nuance lives in their language. You can run a room of legal buyers, ask the sharp question, and write a specification precise enough to build from. Other EU languages are a plus.


Why us?

  • Impact over hype. You define a new discipline at the intersection of law, product, and AI. Your work directly shapes how thousands of legal professionals will operate.
  • No silos. You sit between Product, Engineering, and the customer, with a direct line to all three. The better argument wins, not the higher title.
  • We invest in you. The enterprise motion (multi-stakeholder pilots, procurement cycles, security reviews) is teachable, and we teach it: side by side in real customer calls from week one.
  • Real ownership. Competitive salary and employee stock options (ESOP).
  • Build in public. We want you to keep publishing what you build, because it makes you better and it makes us visible.
  • Offices in Berlin, Leipzig, and Zurich with a flexible hybrid setup. Regular apéros, lunches, and hiking trips as we enjoy the journey together.


Process

  1. Expectations. A conversation with the People Manager about the role and who you are.
  2. Depth. A conversation with our General Counsel & Head of Legal AI on Legal Engineering at Legartis and where the legal market is going.
  3. Build session. A live case at the intersection of legal reasoning, prompting, and product work: a real customer scenario, a legal AI workflow, or a playbook that misbehaves.
  4. Meet the team in our Zurich office.
  5. A mutual decision, before we welcome you to the team.

We set the standard for AI-powered contract review. Today we build a holistic platform that changes how legal teams operate from review to negotiation, powered by our Legal Agent. We are looking for the person who makes that value real for customers: in the demo, in onboarding, and inside the AI itself.

When you join Legartis, you don't just take a job, you take ownership. We are a team of product builders and legal experts. We don't chase hype; we build substance.


Your mission

This is not a classic legal role, and not a classic sales or product role. You operate at the intersection of Law, Revenue, and AI, where you are a lever, not a bottleneck: your job is to build the demos, playbooks, and standards that let the whole company scale, and to step into the calls where your expertise closes the gap.

1. Commercial impact. You help win and grow customers. You build and run demos that create a "wow" moment, join high-stakes prospect calls as the legal expert who speaks at eye level with GCs, and run our trials and workshops: onboarding sessions where customers solve their own use cases live, with you coaching. You turn objections into use cases and interest into next steps, and you enable our Sales team to tell the legal story without you in the room. You think of outcomes in terms of trial-to-signature conversion, adoption, expansion.

2. Customer transformation. Once a deal is signed, you make the value real by acting as a strategic sparring partner in onboarding: defining review requirements, tuning playbooks and prompts, and showing legal teams where Legartis delivers the highest ROI. You turn individual learnings into scalable standards and documentation.

3. Making the AI better. You work hands-on with the Legal Agent: prompting, testing, diagnosing where it breaks and why. You feed what you learn from customers back into Product and Engineering (playbook quality, test sets, edge cases) so the product improves with every customer.

4. Internal legal support. You don't just sell the tool; you use it. When necessary, you support Legartis as in-house counsel on contract reviews and specific legal questions.


Your profile

We are honest: people who combine all of this are rare. We hire for aptitude and attitude, assess hands-on in a case study, and train the rest side by side, in real customer work.

1. You can sell the product (key). Not in the cold-calling sense, but in the way a great expert sells: by making the customer succeed in front of their own team. Concretely, this means you can (or want to learn to):

  • Run a live demo with confidence including customized, high-stakes demos and recover gracefully when something doesn't land: pull out a better prompt, adjust on the spot, turn a skeptical question into a stronger result.

  • Speak at eye level with GCs and legal teams asking sharp discovery questions, translating their friction points into what the product can do, and framing value in their language (ROI, risk, time saved).
  • Always leave with a next step. Trial licenses, a hackathon, a follow-up workshop, a scoped rollout conversation. We've spent years watching talented engineering teams lose momentum to the same frustrating bottleneck: waiting. Waiting for CI to finish. Waiting for builds to complete. Waiting for tests to run.

Something that would seamlessly integrate with our workflows and the tools teams already love—but make everything dramatically faster and more cost-effective.

Namespace's approach is low-friction, designed for immediate integration into existing developer toolchains, empowering teams to experience tangible results within just five minutes. With an end-to-end stack optimized for high performance—including compute, memory, storage, and networking—Namespace delivers capabilities and efficiencies unmatched by traditional cloud providers.

Own the software that drives our hardware. You'll write the control planes, automation, and observability that keep our global fleet fast, efficient, and reliable, while charting a path to scale that continues to increase the number of "machines under management" per engineer.

Our culture

We're looking for people with grit—people who push through ambiguity, take ownership, and keep going when things get hard. You're deeply curious, driven to understand how things work and how they can be improved. Most importantly, you have a strong bias to execution: you don't wait for perfect conditions, you ship, learn, and iterate quickly. If you care about building, moving fast, and making real impact, you'll fit right in.

What you'll do

  • Manage and automate the fleet – build services for provisioning, health checks, upgrades, and incident remediation

  • Uphold reliability – embed observability, graceful degradation, and rollback paths into every layer you touch

  • Architect the network – design and evolve a high-throughput, low-latency fabric tailored to our high performance use-cases

  • Ship software, not scripts – develop clean, testable code (mostly Go) that treats our fleet like a first-class API

  • Drive efficiency – improve utilization and power-to-performance ratios so capacity grows slower than usage

  • Partner across the stack – work with product, infra, and platform teams to scope and deliver features like storage-aware scheduling, cache volumes, and other developer-facing features

What we're looking for

  • Proven experience engineering large-scale infrastructure - writing the software that runs fleets, not just operating existing hyperscalers

  • Depth in network architecture, data-center design, and performance tuning

  • Hands-on time deploying and managing compute hardware at scale (servers, switches, etc)

  • A track record of delivering reliable systems and measurable efficiency gains

You can expect:

  • Flexible working hours

  • Market-leading parental leave

Life at Namespace Labs:

  • We pride ourselves in being a small team of experts that can achieve a lot.

  • We balance our long-term vision with short-term pragmatism.

title: Brand Manager
description:
About Flink

Flink Robotics delivers superhuman physical work. We are a Zürich-based deep tech startup developing a physics-based world model that lets machines reason about the physical world and do work robots couldn't do before - starting with logistics.

We're a team of engineers and researchers with roots at ETH Zürich, backed by leading European investors. The technology is ambitious; now we want the way we look and show up to match it.

The role

You make Flink look as cool from the outside as it is on the inside. As our first brand & marketing hire, you own how Flink shows up to the world and help shape how it feels to work here.

This is a hands-on role with a lot of ownership from day one. You'll work directly with the CEO and the whole team, and you'll have real freedom to set the tone. We care more about taste, energy and drive than years of experience; junior profiles are very welcome.

What you'll do

  • Own our look and feel. Evolve and guard Flink's visual identity. Logo use, colours, typography, photo and video style: and make sure everything we put out is consistent.

  • Run our website. Keep flink.so fresh, fast and on-message: new pages, news, job posts, visuals. Work with freelancers or agencies where needed.

  • Build our social presence. Plan and create content for LinkedIn and other channels. Robot footage, behind-the-scenes, team stories, milestones and grow an audience that gets excited about what we do.

  • Run marketing campaigns. Turn our story into campaigns, from product launches and trade fair pushes to customer and recruiting campaigns. You own the creative and the message, and work closely with the Growth team on goals, audiences and channels.

  • Tell our story visually. Create or coordinate photos, videos, graphics and animations of our robots and technology. Support pitch decks, investor updates and sales materials so they look world-class.

  • Organise events. From trade fairs and demo days to meetups, customer visits and team events. Plan them, run them and make them memorable.

  • Make our space amazing. Shape how our office and workshop look and feel, so every visitor - investor, customer or candidate - gets the Flink vibe.

  • Strengthen our employer brand. Help us attract top engineers: careers page, job ads, recruiting content, how candidates experience Flink.

title: Controller
description:
About Notabene

Notabene is building infrastructure that's transforming how money moves in the digital economy. We're evolving beyond our compliance foundations to enable the next generation of digital financial services between regulated institutions with unprecedented efficiency. Location:

US-based, Remote East Coast

The impact you will have

Notabene is planning on going through its first external financial statement audit, covering the fiscal years ending January 2026 and January 2027. You will own that process. You will also own the close, the books, and the accounting policy for a two-entity, multi-currency business whose revenue includes subscription fees, usage-based transaction billing, and a payments network take rate that has no clean accounting precedent anywhere.

The accounting function is already substantially built. Close runs, the books are in order, and readiness work for the audit is well underway. What we need is someone to own it, finish it, and take it through the audit, while raising the standard on policy and documentation as the business gets more complex. You will be the most senior accounting voice in the company, reporting to the VP of Finance, with one direct report and a set of external providers. You will not have a large team before late 2027, and that is deliberate. Capacity here comes from better systems and better automation, and you will be the one deciding what those look like.

Within a year you are successful if

  • Notabene has a clean audit opinion on both fiscal years, with no material weaknesses and no second cycle on auditor requests

  • The close hits its calendar consistently, starting with the revenue close landing on time

  • Revenue recognition is documented in a written memo that stands up in fieldwork, rather than living only in the billing system configuration

  • Multi-entity consolidation and FX translation run cleanly enough to survive audit scrutiny, with intercompany and CTA tied and supported

  • Payroll allocation across departments and software development capitalization are written policy applied consistently, not judgment applied after the fact

  • Key accounting controls are documented, operating, and evidenced

  • At least two accounting processes that are manual today run without a person in the loop, and still hold up under audit

What you will be doing

Audit. Run the readiness assessment, build the remediation plan, contribute the technical view on which firm we engage, and then own the auditor relationship day to day.

Close and reporting. Own the monthly, quarterly, and annual close across Notabene Inc. and Notabene GmbH. Produce GAAP financial statements, consolidations, intercompany eliminations, and FX translation under ASC 830.

Technical accounting. Write the positions and the memos. ASC 606 across three revenue models, ASC 350-40 for internal-use software capitalization, ASC 718 for stock compensation expense, and whatever emerges as stablecoin payment revenue matures.

Revenue and billing systems. Own Tabs as the billing and revenue system of record, including contract configuration, usage data integrity, and the bridge from Tabs to the general ledger.

Cost accounting. Build the payroll allocation method for people whose work splits across functions, and the capitalization policy for development work, so departmental margin reflects where effort actually goes.

Controls. Design and implement controls over revenue, cash, procure to pay, and payroll. Not SOX. Controls that operate, are evidenced, and can be walked by an auditor.

Automation. Evaluate the accounting stack and the processes running on it with a bias toward automation, including agentic tooling where work is rule-bound and high volume. Categorization, reconciliation matching, usage validation, and collections follow-up are the obvious places to start.

Accounting operations. Own AR and collections with your direct report, plus AP and payroll accounting. Employee onboarding and HRIS administration sit with People, not with you.

Tax. Own US tax compliance in coordination with our external advisers, including the income tax provision and sales tax. Coordinate Swiss compliance with our local accountants.

External providers. We produce revenue in-house, our Swiss accountants produce their piece, and our outsourced firm assembles the close. You will own the checklist, the policies, and the reconciliations, so providers execute against a Notabene-owned close rather than holding it themselves.

What you bring

  • Experience as a Controller, Assistant Controller, or Senior Accounting Manager at a venture-backed company, with a track record of raising the standard on process rather than just running what exists

  • You have taken a company through a first external audit and can describe specifically what broke and what you did about it

  • Month-end close ownership across two or more legal entities in different currencies

  • Deep, hands-on ASC 606, applied to at least one revenue model without clean precedent, and defended to an auditor

  • You operate in the detail. You build the calendar, do the reconciliations, and touch the ledger

  • Experience developing a small team or a single direct report

Nice to have

  • Active CPA license

  • Usage-based or consumption billing experience, particularly Tabs, Metronome, Maxio, or similar

  • Public accounting background, especially audit

  • Software development capitalization under ASC 350-40, including the time capture that makes it auditable

  • Experience replacing manual accounting work with automation, and a clear view on what should stay manual

  • Swiss entity experience, including CHF functional currency and Swiss statutory or VAT exposure

  • Digital assets, payments, or regulated financial services exposure

Benefits

Flexible Remote Work: Work from anywhere! $1000 WFH Stipend: Use within your first year of employment. MacBook Pro: Procured by you and your manager to find a model that meets your needs. Unlimited PTO: We trust you to take as much holiday as you need. Country-Specific Benefits: Statutory offerings and contributions, managed via our employer-of-record.

Test, Metrology, and Automation

• Experience with precision optical alignment, opto-mechanical systems, packaging, and system integration.

title: Senior Backend Engineer(Go), Storage Platform
description:
About Wolt

At Wolt, we create technology that brings joy, simplicity and earnings to the neighborhoods of the world. In 2014 we started with delivery of restaurant food. Now we're building the delivery of (almost) everything and you'll find us in over 500 cities in 30 countries around the world. In 2022 we joined forces with DoorDash and together we keep on dreaming big and expanding across the globe.

Working at Wolt isn't always easy, but it's definitely exciting. Here you'll learn more, build more, and ship more than in most other companies. You'll be challenged a lot, but also have a lot of fun on the way. So, if you're a self-starter with drive and entrepreneurial spirit, this could be the ride of your life.

What you'll be doing

As part of Wolt's Platform department (Core Group), you'll help improve and automate operations for our storage access platform - our real time database abstraction layer solution designed with scale and resiliency in mind . The product you will build enforces best practices by design, abstracts database infrastructure, and supports Multi-Region architecture through data sharding and replication. You join a team of highly skilled engineers in designing, building and optimizing this platform and ensuring smooth developer onboarding, constant improvement and optimization. 

As an engineer on the Storage access platform team, you'll work on platform features such as UI for developer teams, storage abstraction layer, database automation, client SDK and proxy, Change Data Capture pipelines, caching and ephemeral storage, Hot & Cold storage management and more.

Our humble expectations

You'll be a great fit for this role if you have the following skills and experience:

  • A strong developer-to-developer mindset, with a genuine enjoyment of building for internal customers and treating other engineers as your primary users.
  • Adaptability and strong motivation for working with distributed systems.
  • A data-driven approach to decision-making and a collaborative mindset, with the ability to navigate disagreements constructively and deliver consistently.
  • Autonomy in dynamic, fast-paced environments with frequent change.
  • A product- and platform-oriented approach to engineering challenges.
  • Excellent communication skills, with the ability to engage effectively with stakeholders and cross-functional teams.
  • A collaborative spirit and experience contributing to diverse and inclusive work environments.

Technical proficiencies:

  • Expertise in NoSQL databases, particularly Cassandra or DynamoDB.
  • Experience with large-scale distributed systems, emphasizing both velocity and scalability.
  • Familiarity with SRE principles; however, a background in Backend Development is essential.
  • Practical knowledge of Kubernetes, including EKS, as an end user.

You don't need to tick every box, but if you see yourself in many of these points, we'd love to hear from you!


What we offer

At Wolt, we're committed to building an environment where engineers can make an impact while enjoying meaningful challenges. As a member of the the team you'll enjoy:

  • Working on solutions that support millions of users
  • Solving complex problems in performance, reliability and automation
  • A collaborative and inclusive culture that supports your professional and personal well-being

We also offer flexible work arrangements, competitive compensation, and ongoing learning opportunities to help you thrive.

 

Our Commitment to Diversity and Inclusion

We're committed to growing and empowering a more inclusive community within our company, industry, and cities. That's why we hire and cultivate diverse teams of people from all backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives. We believe that true innovation happens when everyone has room at the table and the tools, resources, and opportunity to excel.

Beware of recruitment scams: DoorDash, Deliveroo, and Wolt will never ask you to pay money or share sensitive financial information during hiring — learn more about our legitimate recruiting process at Recruitment Scam Awareness - DoorDash .

description:
Über uns

Die FP Pro­duk­ti­ons- und Vertriebs-GmbH, ein Un­ter­neh­men der welt­weit tä­ti­gen Tata Grup­pe, ist ein füh­ren­der An­bie­ter von in­no­va­ti­ven und hoch­wer­ti­gen Bau­kom­po­nen­ten für die in­dus­tri­el­le und ge­werb­li­che Bau­wei­se.   • Betreuung von Bauteilversuchen sowie Herstellung und Begleitung von Versuchselementen

Was Sie mitbringen sollten:

  • Abgeschlossene Berufsausbildung im technischen Bereich, idealerweise in der Metallindustrie oder Bauelemente- bzw. Baustoffindustrie

  • Erste Erfahrungen im Bereich Qualitätssicherung oder Labor, idealerweise bei Sandwichelementen oder vergleichbaren Produkten

  • Kenntnisse im Umgang mit Prüftechnik und Laborequipment

  • Gute PC-Kenntnisse (MS Office, idealerweise Zwick/TestXpert oder vergleichbare Prüfsoftware)

  • Technisches Verständnis für Werkstoffe (Metall, PIR, Mineralwolle) von Vorteil

  • Sorgfältige, analytische und strukturierte Arbeitsweise

  • Teamfähigkeit, Zuverlässigkeit sowie ausgeprägtes Qualitäts- und Sicherheitsbewusstsein

  • Bereitschaft zur Arbeit im Schichtbetrieb

Was wir bieten:

  • Eine interessante Tätigkeit innerhalb eines internationalen Konzernumfeldes

  • Eine der Aufgabenstellung entsprechende Vergütung

  • Individuelle Weiterbildungsmöglichkeiten

  • Corporate Benefits

In den ersten sechs Monaten Ihrer Probezeit lernen Sie unsere Abläufe, Fertigungsanlagen und das Qualitätsmanagement-Team in Netphen im Detail kennen. title: Founders Associate (m/w/d)
description:
Bei uns gibt es mehr zu tun als Hände. Wir geben dir Einblick und Verantwortung ab Tag eins, du findest die Lösungen und setzt sie um.

Meerbusch, überwiegend vor Ort mit Flexibilität · unbefristet · Vollzeit · ab sofort

Hier fängt gerade etwas an, und du kannst von Anfang an dabei sein. Du baust mit an Orten, an denen du selbst gern wärst. Hier macht deine Arbeit einen Unterschied, den man sieht, und gute Arbeit wird bei uns anerkannt und bezahlt. Jeder Monat bringt dich ein Stück weiter, mit Menschen, die du magst. Wie groß das wird, liegt an uns.

Worum es geht

Wir sind acht Leute und betreiben Anlagen im Bergischen Land, auf denen rund 350 Menschen ein kleines Haus haben. Gerade bauen wir daneben etwas Neues auf: ein anderes Produkt, neue Orte, eine neue Marke.

Das Problem dabei ist sehr konkret. Der Geschäftsführer verbringt seine Tage mit Betriebskostenfragen und Pächterfällen, statt an dem zu arbeiten, was uns nach vorne bringt. Und unsere beiden Kolleginnen in Verwaltung und Buchhaltung sind die einzigen Menschen für ihre Themen.

Genau da kommst du rein. Nicht als Aushilfe, sondern als der Mensch, der Dinge übernimmt und dann selbst besser macht.

Was du machst

Dein erstes großes Projekt suchst du dir selbst aus. In den ersten zwei Wochen wählst du aus sechs Themen, die uns alle weiterbringen: unser selbst gebautes Verwaltungssystem mit Lovable oder etwas Besserem weiterentwickeln, die Betriebskostenabrechnung durch KI automatisieren, unsere Finanzen strukturieren und auf Optimierungsbedarf analysieren, eine Vertriebspipeline aufsetzen, Abläufe verbessern oder unseren Vermarktungsauftritt bauen. Was nach sechs Monaten fertig sein soll, legen wir gemeinsam fest.

Daneben hältst du den Alltag am Laufen und unterstützt den Geschäftsführer bei unterschiedlichen Projekten. Du wirst seine rechte Hand: Du bereitest Entscheidungen vor, rechnest durch, baust Übersichten wie unser Finanz-Dashboard und die Cashflow-Planung aus, stellst Unterlagen zusammen, fasst nach und bringst Dinge zu Ende, die sonst liegen bleiben.

Und du lernst die ganze Firma kennen. Du arbeitest dich so weit in Verwaltung und Buchhaltung ein, dass du unsere Kolleginnen vertreten kannst, wenn sie im Urlaub sind oder ausfallen. Heute gibt es bei uns für keine Aufgabe eine zweite Person. Und wo du siehst, dass ihnen etwas die Arbeit leichter machen würde, zeigst du es ihnen.

Außerdem hältst du unserer Kollegin oder unserem Kollegen für die Standorte den Rücken frei. Diese Rolle besetzen wir gerade neu: Sie gestaltet unsere Anlagen, richtet Häuser her und verkauft sie. Damit das draußen stattfinden kann, übernimmst du, was daran im Büro anfällt: Termine, Unterlagen, Behördenwege, Nachfassen.

Und die Website gehört dir. Aufbau, Inhalte, Pflege, Weiterentwicklung. Wie die Marke aussieht und klingt, entscheiden wir. Sichtbar machen wirst du sie.

KI ist dabei dein Werkzeug, nicht dein Bonus. Wir arbeiten damit, wo es geht, und erwarten von dir dasselbe.

Und ja, es gibt auch Bürobedarf zu bestellen und die Weihnachtsfeier zu organisieren. Bei acht Leuten macht das jeder mal. Es ist nicht der Kern der Stelle, aber es kommt vor, und wir sagen es lieber vorher.

Was du nicht machst

Bankgespräche führen, Markenentscheidungen treffen, Zahlungen freigeben. Das bleibt im ersten Jahr bei der Geschäftsführung. Vorbereiten und mitdenken wirst du überall.

Wer du bist

Uns interessiert weniger, was du schon gemacht hast, als wie du bist. Ein Studium hilft, ein bestimmtes ist nicht nötig, Berufserfahrung ist kein Kriterium.

Was zählt: Du bist neugierig und lernst schnell. Du kannst mit Technik und mit KI umgehen oder willst es dringend lernen. Du kannst mit Zahlen umgehen und einen Finanzplan lesen, oder du willst es lernen. Du willst verstehen, wie die Finanzen eines Unternehmens wirklich aussehen, und du glaubst keiner Zahl, die du nicht geprüft hast. Du machst Dinge fertig. Du hörst zu und lässt dir etwas sagen, ohne dich klein zu machen. Du sagst Hallo und Tschüss und scheust dich nicht, bei Bedarf auch mal das Telefon in die Hand zu nehmen, um etwas vorwärtszubringen.

Was du bekommst

Einblick in alles. Zahlen, Verträge, Strategie, Personal. Du sitzt neben dem Geschäftsführer und siehst, wie Entscheidungen zustande kommen. Das bekommst du in einem Konzern nach fünf Jahren nicht.

Verantwortung schneller, als dir lieb ist. Bei acht Leuten gibt es keine Warteschleife. Was du kannst, machst du.

Jemanden, der dich coacht. Du wirst nicht ins kalte Wasser geworfen und dann alleingelassen. Wir nehmen uns Zeit, und wir sagen dir ehrlich, was gut läuft und was nicht.

Eine Rolle, die mit dir wächst. Wir wissen heute nicht genau, wo du in zwei Jahren stehst. Das hängt davon ab, was du dir holst.

Wie wir arbeiten

Wir reden Klartext, auch wenn es unangenehm ist. Widerspruch mit Begründung ist willkommen, besonders gegenüber der Geschäftsführung. Wir arbeiten lieber pragmatisch als perfekt. Fehler sind in Ordnung, solange man sie ausspricht und daraus lernt.

Bewerbung

Kein Anschreiben. Und bitte keine Bewerbung, die eine KI für dich geschrieben hat. Wir wollen dich kennenlernen, nicht ein Sprachmodell. Dass du mit KI umgehen kannst, ist uns wichtig, aber im Job und nicht in der Bewerbung.

Eine Sprachnachricht, etwa eine Minute. Erzähl uns von etwas, das du selbst aufgebaut oder organisiert hast, und sag uns, was wir sonst über dich wissen sollten. Einmal einsprechen reicht, wir erwarten kein Tonstudio.

Dazu deinen Lebenslauf, deine Gehaltsvorstellung und einen Satz dazu, wann du könntest.

We’re venture-backed, early-stage, and building a team that blends deep clinical expertise with engineering intensity—moving with the rigor the medical field demands and the speed the problem deserves.

title: Forward Deployed Inference Engineer

The role sits at the intersection of model architecture, inference performance, systems optimization, developer tooling, and customer deployment. You will work hands-on with engineering while also acting as a technical bridge to Product, BizDev, Sales, and customers.

  • Turn customer workloads into fast, credible performance answers through profiling & benchmarking. Define relevant KPIs, compare against competitive baselines, and keep our evaluation methodology current with external benchmarks.

  • Turn repeated customer-specific learnings into reusable tooling, documentation, benchmarks, or product improvements.

Core qualifications

  • Strong hands-on experience with AI models and inference systems, especially dense and MoE LLMs (Llama, DeepSeek, Qwen, GPT-OSS, Kimi, GLM), and VLM, speech and diffusion models.
  • Strong Python and PyTorch skills and the ability to understand and modify model code.
  • Experience profiling, benchmarking, or optimizing model inference and reasoning about latency, throughput, memory, and utilization.
  • Strong problem-solving and communication skills, with the ability to drive ambiguous technical problems across team boundaries.

Strong pluses

  • Experience with LLM serving and deployment stacks such as vLLM, SGLang, or similar systems.

  • Experience bringing models up on new accelerators or non-standard hardware, including performance debugging across framework/runtime/hardware boundaries.
  • Practical experience with production inference techniques or environments such as quantization, distributed inference, or Kubernetes.
  • Experience navigating and contributing to Rust codebases.

Tensordyne Values

  • Think big. Pursue ambitious technical and business goals.
  • Aim for excellence. Quality matters in everything we build and deliver.

  • Operate with integrity. Be direct, transparent, and respectful.
  • Win as a team. Make the people around you more effective.

Wir bauen bei Aampere gerade eine Marke von 0 auf. Bisher kommen über 95 % unserer Kunden aus Growth Marketing und unsere Brand Awareness bei EV-Fahrern liegt bei ca. 5 bis 10 %.
Da wir eine starke B2C-Brand aufbauen wollen, wissen wir, dass wir früh in Brand investieren müssen. Wer in Deutschland ein E-Auto verkaufen will, soll automatisch an Aampere denken und wir suchen die Person, die das für uns umsetzt.
Die Strategie legst du mit dem Head of Marketing fest. Die Umsetzung liegt komplett bei dir, ohne Micro-Management im Tagesgeschäft.

Du planst die Kampagnen und führst sie auch durch. Du entscheidest Umfang, Region, Kanäle und Botschaft, von OOH über YouTube bis PR und Community. Nichts ist vorentschieden. Du testest Regionen gegeneinander und skalierst, was gewinnt.
Du bestimmst, wofür Aampere steht. Aus Research zu Kunden, Markt und Wettbewerb entstehen Positionierung, Narrative und Tone of Voice. Das Fundament gibt es noch nicht, aber die Research dafür würde schon gestartet.
Du denkst über Awareness Kanäle hinaus. Ein großer Teil unserer Brand Wahrnehmung entsteht während des Sales Prozesses. Du denkst vom ersten bis zum letzten Touchpoint der Customer Journey und sorgst in den richtigen Momenten für die richtige Message & Erfahrung.
Du bekommst ein sechsstelliges Budget. Wir planen ein festes Budget für Brand in 2027 ein. Wohin wir es investieren, liegt komplett bei dir.


Das bringst du mit

Du hast eine Brand von null mitgebaut. 4 bis 6 Jahre Brand-Erfahrung im B2C, Startup oder startup-nah. Du hast nicht ein bereits bestehendes System verwaltet, sondern eines aufgebaut.
Du denkst von Konzept bis Go-Live. Du hast Multi-Channel-Kampagnen bereits selbst konzipiert und live gebracht. Du weißt genau, wann welcher Kanal der richtige ist und wie wir unsere Message gezielt an die Kunden übermitteln. Du musst dabei nicht jeden Schritt selbst ausführen, sondern kannst auch auf externe Ressourcen zurückgreifen.
Du hast kreative Ideen und verstehst, weshalb sie funktionieren. Wir suchen die Person, die auf Sachen kommt, an die im Growth-Team niemand denkt. Zeig uns eine Kampagne, die es ohne dich nicht gegeben hätte und was danach messbar anders war.

Late Dinner im Office: Wenn es abends länger wird, übernehmen wir dein Dinner (Uber Eats)

title: Senior Product Developer – Candy & Confectionery (All Genders)

We are looking for a Senior Product Developer for Candy & Confectionery to own the technical development of our portfolio from the first brief through formulation, sensory validation, scale-up and launch.

As our Senior Product Developer, you will bring technical depth to one of our most important categories and make sure every decision works in the real world: in the recipe, in the factory and in the customer’s hands.

Are you a food developer who knows how to turn a great idea into a product people genuinely love? YOUR TASKS

  • Sensory, Shelf Life & Scale-Up: You plan and coordinate sensory, shelf-life and stability testing. You prepare for pilot and industrial trials, work closely with co-manufacturers, troubleshoot issues and follow solutions through to production.

  • Specifications, Suppliers & Compliance: You manage formulations, specifications, technical documentation, ingredients and samples. Together with our Quality team, you ensure that food law, labelling, allergen, nutritional and claims requirements are considered from the start.

  • Cross-Functional Ownership: You work closely with Product, Quality, Operations, Procurement, Brand, Retail and Marketing. You communicate clearly, flag risks early, challenge assumptions and keep projects moving.

YOUR PROFILE

  • You bring 5+ years of experience in food product development, R&D, or NPD, with a track record from brief through formulation, sensory validation, scale-up, and launch. Hands-on experience in gummies, candy, chocolate, confectionery, or a related sweet-goods category is mandatory.

  • You understand how taste, texture, processing, stability, shelf life, ingredients and production realities come together in a successful product. You have experience with sugar-reduction or no-added-sugar systems and know how to balance product performance with consumer expectations.

  • You have worked with ingredient suppliers and co-manufacturers and have been involved in pilot or industrial-scale production. You are comfortable with specifications, technical documentation, and food-law requirements.

  • You take ownership and follow through. You are structured without being bureaucratic, comfortable with ambiguity and willing to challenge a brief, assumption or timeline when needed. You communicate clearly with both technical and non-technical stakeholders and enjoy working as a senior individual contributor without direct reports initially.

WHAT MAKES YOUR PROFILE COMPLETE

  • Experience launching 10+ food products, ideally across multiple markets.

  • Experience working with gummies, candy, chocolate bars, cookies, filled confectionery or similar products.

  • Strong knowledge of sugar reduction, sweetener systems, fibres and texture management.

  • Experience planning, conducting or interpreting sensory tests, shelf-life studies and stability testing.

  • Background in better-for-you food, functional food, private-label NPD, or a fast-growing consumer brand.

  • Experience delivering products into D2C and retail channels across DACH or Europe.


AND WHY AHEAD?

Working at ahead is more than just a job - it’s your opportunity to develop as a professional and as a person, while shaping the future of snacking. Our mission is to make low sugar the new standard, and we pour that ambition into every product we create. You’ll become part of a team where international talent, startup drive, real impact, and true ownership come together.

  • Hypergrowth Environment: If you're looking for greenfield, creative freedom, and real impact, you're in the right place. We're a team that is scaling fast - with purpose
  • Great Workspace: A central office in the heart of Hamburg near the Alster, top equipment (MacBook), snacks, drinks, plenty of ahead products - and yes, a ping-pong table. We’re also pet-friendly, so you can always bring your furry friend along
  • Amazing Team: Young, international, ambitious - inspiring colleagues who collaborate, support each other, and genuinely enjoy working together

Glasgow
